newsitem.title: ITALY: More Mafiosi charged in 1992 killing of judge.
newsitem.headline: More Mafiosi charged in 1992 killing of judge.

text.p: Police on Tuesday arrested four more people suspected of involvement in the 1992 killing of an anti-Mafia judge in Sicily and told 24 Mafiosi already jailed on other charges that they too were suspected.
Magistrates told a news conference the arrests and warrants were part of a continuing investigation into the car bomb killing of magistrate Paolo Borsellino and five bodyguards in July 1992.

Borsellino was killed two months after star anti-Mafia magistrate Giovanni Falcone was blown up along with his wife and three bodyguards by a bomb planted under a highway outside the Sicilian capital, Palermo.
A first trial for the Borsellino bombing ended in January with the conviction of four lower level Mafiosi accused of carrying out the killing.
A second trial began last month with 18 defendants including boss of bosses Salvatore "Toto" Riina, who was arrested in 1993.
The four men arrested on Tuesday were low level Mafiosi.
One, Giuseppe Biondo, was suspected of preparing the remote control device which set off the car bomb. The other three were suspected of having provided shelter for Mafiosi.
Among the 24 in jail who were advised they were suspected of involvement in the Borsellino killing were former leading Mafia bosses Benedetto "Nitto" Santapaola and Giovanni Brusca.
Brusca, one of the Mafia's bloodthirstiest members, is among more than 40 people on trial over the Falcone murder and is accused of having detonated the bomb which killed him.
